title: Isom sheaf between constant finitely presented modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $M,N$ be finitely presented $\Lambda$-modules (each is the cokernel of a linear map $\Lambda^a\to\Lambda^b$ for finite integers $a,b\geq0$). Write $\underline M,\underline N,\underline\Lambda$ for constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with their module structures [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $\mathcal I$ on an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ to be the set of isomorphisms of $\underline\Lambda|_U$-module sheaves $\underline M|_U\to\underline N|_U$ on the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with restriction by further localization. This is a sheaf of sets. The canonical map $\underline{\operatorname{Isom}_\Lambda(M,N)}\to\mathcal I$, sending a constant module isomorphism to its constant sheaf isomorphism, is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets.

source.place: Tag 093T, lemma-locally-constant, part (2); Isom is defined in its proof as mutually inverse pairs of internal Hom sections.

proof.text: Use the explicit presheaf of actual isomorphisms between F(M) and F(N) on ringed slices. Its restriction is the canonical conjugation by overFunctorMap, so the equivalences with the required slice isomorphisms are identity equivalences. It is a sheaf because local forward maps and inverse maps glue in the two local Hom sheaves.

Apply local injectivity of the constant Hom comparison to M→N and to both endomorphism modules, since finite presentation implies finite generation. Apply local surjectivity to M→N and N→M using finite presentation of the two sources. The generic inverse-pair argument then proves that the constant Isom presheaf map to the local Isom sheaf is locally bijective.

Extend this canonical presheaf map to the constant set sheaf by sheafifyLift. The equation toSheafify_sheafifyLift identifies its composite with the set-sheafification unit with the original constant Isom map. Because the unit is locally bijective, the induced sheaf morphism is locally bijective too. The Mathlib criterion Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso makes it an isomorphism. Evaluate the factorization equation on a constant isomorphism to obtain precisely the stated canonical-section formula.
